title: Mapterhorn pipeline over GEM-15: three test areas
description:
**An experiment, and not a Mapterhorn release.** Three small terrain-tile archives built by running GEM-15 elevation COGs through the [Mapterhorn](https://mapterhorn.com/) terrain pipeline, from an **unmerged fork** at [cholmes/mapterhorn, branch `gem-15-source`](https://github.com/cholmes/mapterhorn/tree/gem-15-source) (archives built at commit `86d8494`, forked from upstream `main` at `2c4195d`). The Mapterhorn project has not reviewed, merged or endorsed any of this, and no pull request was opened upstream. Nothing here is Mapterhorn data. The pipeline code is BSD-3-licensed and is credited as a tool, not as a publisher.

**Why it exists.** Mapterhorn issue [#368](https://github.com/mapterhorn/mapterhorn/issues/368), "Thoughts on Google's GEM-15 being used as the baseline model?", records a maintainer suggesting that somebody "run the Mapterhorn terrain pipeline with some of the google tiffs". This collection is that run, for three areas chosen to answer a specific question: what does a global 15 m optical source actually add to a terrain archive whose deepest zoom is decided by a resolution rule?

**The answer, which is the point of the experiment.** Mapterhorn's `get_smallest_overzoom` picks the first zoom whose 512 px Web Mercator tile pixel fully samples the source, then clamps up to z12. A ground pixel of 15 m occupies 15 / cos(latitude) metres of EPSG:3857, and the z12 tile pixel is 19.11 m, so a 15 m source only crosses into z13 below about 38.3 degrees of latitude. Over Catalonia, GEM-15 therefore produces z12, the same depth the pipeline already produces there from 30 m Copernicus GLO-30: finer content inside the tiles, no extra zoom level. Over Cusco and the High Atlas, both below that latitude, GEM-15 produces z13, one level deeper than Mapterhorn publishes in those places today. A depth equivalent to z14 is unreachable for a 15 m source under this rule at any latitude.

**The three areas.** Catalonia (4 one-degree GEM-15 cells, z12) covers Barcelona, Montserrat and the Sau reservoir, and overlaps this catalog's own terrain demo so the two can be compared. Cusco in Peru (1 cell, z13) and the High Atlas around Toubkal in Morocco (1 cell, z13) were picked because Mapterhorn production holds no source finer than GLO-30 there, which was verified against Mapterhorn's own published coverage index, its archive manifest and its attribution list.

**Two bands per area, so six archives.** Each area ships the GEM-15 surface model (DSM) and its bare-earth model (DTM), built from the same cells by the same pipeline and pixel-aligned. The DTM is the closer analog to Mapterhorn's own production sources, which are national bare-earth models serving cartographic terrain, so it is the fairer answer to the question the issue asked. The DSM stays the like-for-like comparison against Copernicus GLO-30, which is itself a surface model. Treat the DTM as the more experimental band: GEM-15 predicts it from the DSM with a model trained on airborne lidar, and it is markedly weaker under closed canopy. The DTM reads at or below the DSM at every probe point measured, but the gap is not a reliable canopy or building height on steep ground, because the two archives are mosaicked and resampled independently.

**Encoding.** Mapzen terrarium in 512 px lossless WebP tiles, PMTiles specification v3, clustered, zoom 0 to the per-area maximum. Decode with elevation = (R * 256 + G + B / 256) − 32768. MapLibre reads each archive as a `raster-dem` source with `"encoding": "terrarium"` and `"tileSize": 512`. Set `maxzoom` per archive: 12 for Catalonia, 13 for Cusco and the High Atlas.

**Void fill, and the licence consequence.** GEM-15 masks water plus a 9 m buffer, so the Sau reservoir is NaN in the source and a naive build renders it as a flat 0 m pit. The fork fills GEM-15's nodata from Copernicus GLO-30 before tiling, with an EGM2008-to-EGM96 geoid correction applied inside the fill and a 3 px feather toward GEM-15's own nearest valid value. Filled pixels are GLO-30 at 30 m, not GEM-15 at 15 m, and nothing in the tiles marks them. Because filled pixels derive from GLO-30, every archive needs the Copernicus modified-data notice below in addition to the GEM-15 attribution.

**Status.** Experimental and frozen. These archives are a point measurement from 2026-11-15, not a maintained layer, and they will not track upstream Mapterhorn or a new GEM-15 release. Use them to draw and to compare, and read the item COGs in the [`gem-15`](../gem-15/collection.json) collection for heights.

Agents should start at [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md); people should start at [README.md](README.md).

terrain-barcelona.title: Catalonia surface terrain tiles, zoom 0 to 12 (terrarium)
terrain-barcelona.description: The GEM-15 **DSM**, its surface band, over 4 one-degree cells in UTM zone 31N (w1s41, w2s41, w3s40, w3s41), covering Barcelona, Montserrat and the Sau reservoir. The matching bare-earth model is `terrain-barcelona-dtm`, built from the same cells by the same pipeline, and the two are pixel-aligned. Terrarium-encoded 512 px lossless WebP tiles, zoom 0 to 12, 10,931 tiles, clustered, PMTiles specification v3. Read it as a MapLibre `raster-dem` source with `"encoding": "terrarium"`, `"tileSize": 512` and `"maxzoom": 12`. Decode a pixel with elevation = (R * 256 + G + B / 256) − 32768. Zoom 12 is the deepest zoom Mapterhorn's own resolution rule allows a 15 m source at this latitude, which is also what the pipeline reaches here from 30 m GLO-30. Do not trust the PMTiles header bounds: the fork's bundle_area.py writes the whole world (-180 to 180, -85.05 to 85.05) into every archive it builds, which is a defect of this experimental build. The tiles actually present span 0 to 5.625 degrees east and 36.598 to 45.089 degrees north, the tile-aligned aggregation blocks the pipeline built, and real GEM-15 elevation exists only over the four one-degree cells inside that footprint. Terrarium has no nodata value, so every other tile in the archive encodes as 0 m. GEM-15's own voids, water plus a 9 m buffer among them, are filled from Copernicus GLO-30 before encoding, converted EGM2008 to EGM96 and feathered toward GEM-15's nearest valid value over 3 px. A filled pixel is GLO-30 at 30 m, not GEM-15 at 15 m, and nothing in the tiles marks it: draw with these, measure with the gem-15 item COGs. Void-filling requires this notice: "produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved". The archive's own PMTiles metadata declares only `attribution`, set by the pipeline to "© Mapterhorn", which is the tool credit and not the data attribution: a client must state the GEM-15 and Copernicus notices itself.
terrain-barcelona.processing:lineage: Built 2026-11-15 in 9 m 13 s on the forked Mapterhorn pipeline: band 1 of each GEM-15 DSM COG downloaded and extracted (source_gem15_download.py), nodata filled from Copernicus GLO-30 with an EGM2008-to-EGM96 correction and a 3 px feather (source_fill_nodata_glo30.py), bounds written (source_bounds.py), then the pipeline's own unmodified aggregation and downsampling stages, then bundled to one archive (bundle_area.py). Maximum zoom chosen by the pipeline's own get_smallest_overzoom, not set by hand.
